newsitem.title: USA: SBC sues to gain access to long-distance market.
newsitem.headline: SBC sues to gain access to long-distance market.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc. on Wednesday filed a federal lawsuit seeking to overturn provisions in a new telecommunications law restricting Baby Bells from entering long-distance telephone markets, a company lawyer said.

The Baby Bell also planned on Thursday to appeal last week's Federal Communications Commission ruling blocking the company from offering long-distance service in Oklahoma, one of seven states where it operates local calling networks.

In the lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in Wichita Falls, Texas, SBC challenged sections of the Federal Telecommunications Act restricting the regional Baby Bells from offering long-distance calling and other services, attorney Jim Ellis said.
"We are asking the courts to let us compete just like GTE and all these other companies," he said.
The company is not challenging sections of the landmark law that ended monopoly control of local calling markets, opened the markets to rivals and required the Baby Bells to resell services, he said.

The Baby Bells have been barred from entering the $80 billion-a-year national long-distance market since the 1984 breakup of AT&T Corp., and face increased competition for their share of the $100 billion-a-year local-calling business.
SBC's stock closed 6 cents higher at $60.94 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
